verses.1: Now concerning times and moments, brothers, you have no need to be written to,
verses.2: for you yourselves know exactly that the day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night.
verses.3: When they say, "Peace and safety," then sudden destruction will come upon them, as labor pains upon a pregnant woman, and they will not escape.
verses.4: But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that the day may catch you like a thief,
verses.5: for you are all children of the light and children of the day. We are not of the night or of darkness.
verses.6: So then, let us not sleep as the rest do, but let us be alert and sober.
verses.7: For those who sleep, night is for sleeping, and those who get drunk, night is for drunkenness;
verses.8: but we are of the day, so let us be sober, having put on the breastplate of faith and love, and the helmet of the hope of salvation.
verses.9: For God has not destined us for wrath, but for obtaining salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.10: who died for us so that whether we are awake or asleep, we might live together with him.
verses.11: Therefore, encourage one another and build one another up, just as you are doing.
verses.12: We ask you, brothers, to acknowledge those who labor among you and preside over you in the Lord and instruct you,
verses.13: and to respect them very highly in love for their work. Be at peace among yourselves.
verses.14: We also urge you, brothers, to admonish the disorderly, encourage the faint-hearted, help the weak, be patient toward all.
verses.15: See that no one repays evil for evil to anyone, but always pursue what is good, both for one another and for all.
verses.18: in all things give thanks, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
verses.21: but test everything, hold fast what is good,
verses.22: abstain from every kind of evil.
verses.23: Now may the God of peace himself sanctify you completely, and may your whole spirit, soul, and body be kept blameless at the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.24: Faithful is the one who calls you, who will also do it.
verses.26: Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.
verses.27: I charge you by the Lord to have this letter read to all the brothers.
verses.28: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all.

notes:
Notes
- v. 3: “labor pains upon a pregnant woman” is a direct translation of the metaphor, avoiding any euphemistic or archaic phrasing.
- v. 14: “admonish the disorderly” retains the active, corrective tone of the Greek.
- v. 23: “kept blameless at the appearing” reflects the future, eschatological context of παρουσία.
- v. 27: “I charge you by the Lord” reflects the solemnity of ἐνορκίζω, not softened to "I urge" or similar.

[1] Now concerning times and moments, brothers, you have no need to be written to,
[2] for you yourselves know exactly that the day of the Lord comes like a thief in the night.
[3] When they say, "Peace and safety," then sudden destruction will come upon them, as labor pains upon a pregnant woman, and they will not escape.
[4] But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that the day may catch you like a thief,
[5] for you are all children of the light and children of the day. We are not of the night or of darkness.
[6] So then, let us not sleep as the rest do, but let us be alert and sober.
[7] For those who sleep, night is for sleeping, and those who get drunk, night is for drunkenness;
[8] but we are of the day, so let us be sober, having put on the breastplate of faith and love, and the helmet of the hope of salvation.
[9] For God has not destined us for wrath, but for obtaining salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,
[10] who died for us so that whether we are awake or asleep, we might live together with him.
[11] Therefore, encourage one another and build one another up, just as you are doing.
[12] We ask you, brothers, to acknowledge those who labor among you and preside over you in the Lord and instruct you,
[13] and to respect them very highly in love for their work. Be at peace among yourselves.
[14] We also urge you, brothers, to admonish the disorderly, encourage the faint-hearted, help the weak, be patient toward all.
[15] See that no one repays evil for evil to anyone, but always pursue what is good, both for one another and for all.
[16] Always rejoice,
[17] pray without ceasing,
[18] in all things give thanks, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.
[19] Do not quench the Spirit,
[20] do not despise prophecies,
[21] but test everything, hold fast what is good,
[22] abstain from every kind of evil.
[23] Now may the God of peace himself sanctify you completely, and may your whole spirit, soul, and body be kept blameless at the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ.
[24] Faithful is the one who calls you, who will also do it.
[25] Brothers, pray for us.
[26] Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.
[27] I charge you by the Lord to have this letter read to all the brothers.
[28] The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all.

Notes
- v. 3: “labor pains upon a pregnant woman” is a direct translation of the metaphor, avoiding any euphemistic or archaic phrasing.
- v. 14: “admonish the disorderly” retains the active, corrective tone of the Greek.
- v. 23: “kept blameless at the appearing” reflects the future, eschatological context of παρουσία.
- v. 27: “I charge you by the Lord” reflects the solemnity of ἐνορκίζω, not softened to "I urge" or similar.
